feedback: Accepted. The candidate is a well-formed linear achievement RM that mirrors the environment's guaranteed ordering (key_found -> has_matching_key -> target_door_open -> target_room_entered -> target_picked_up), so every progressive transition is schedulable and no event can be skipped: the constraints force key_found strictly before has_matching_key (the key must be in view before pickup), target_door_open strictly after has_matching_key (only the held key unlocks), and target_room_entered/target_picked_up strictly after the door opens, matching u1->u2, u2->u3, u3->u4, u4->u5 exactly. Format follows the paper template exactly: nonempty FINAL_STATES header (u5), declared in STATES and accepting for the task (mission complete on pickup); INITIAL_STATE declared; all transitions reference declared states and every reward triple corresponds to an actual transition. Labels are predicates or else only (no actions, negations, or disjunctions), and each of the six states carries a per-state else self-loop, so irrelevant events (turns, moves, failed toggles, done) are absorbed without state or reward change. Reachability holds: key_found can fire at step 1 in some layouts, and each later milestone is achievable (key, locked door, room, and ball are all reachable; the agent can drop the key before the ball pickup). No stranding despite has_matching_key and target_door_open being flippable conditions: the forward-only chain never deadlocks because the agent must restore has_matching_key to toggle the locked door and can re-open the now-unlocked door keylessly, so pending transitions fire when progress resumes; the latches (key_found, target_room_entered) make each fired transition one-shot, and since the RM never regresses, no reward farming or cycling is possible. Explicit regressions are not required: the task is a monotone achievement chain whose example tasks (find key before opening door, open door before pickup) are enforced by the chain itself. Rewards are dense (every milestone shaped: 0.1/0.2/0.3/0.2/1.0), bounded per transition (<=1.0), all positive, with the terminal reward dominating the sum of intermediates (0.8 < 1.0), and else self-loops implicitly zero so stalling earns nothing. Minor non-blocking observation: the intermediate reward dips from 0.3 (door open) to 0.2 (room entered); this is harmless because transitions are event-forced rather than chosen, though a monotone schedule would be marginally cleaner. No rewrite needed.
